Appendices

Appendix A CUDA Kernel Implementation Details

All CUDA kernels (1,413 lines) are compiled with nvcc -arch=compute_75 and invoked from the Rust engine via FFI wrappers; sources are included with the released implementation.

A.1 F16 →\to Q8 Activation Quantization

The nve_quantize_f16_q8 kernel quantizes F16 activations to INT8 per 32-element group. Grid: (K/32,1)(K/32,1); Block: (32,1)(32,1). (1) Parallel absmax via 5-step log-reduction in shared memory. (2) Scale: s=amax/127.0s=\text{amax}/127.0. (3) Quantize: qi=round​(xi/s)q_{i}=\text{round}(x_{i}/s), clamped to [−127,127][-127,127]. Quantized activations are reused across all matmuls in the same layer.

A.2 W4A8 dp4a Matrix-Vector Product

Grid: (N,1)(N,1); Block: (32,4)=128(32,4)=128 threads; Shared memory: 384 bytes. Each thread processes VDR=2 Q4_0 weight blocks per iteration. Four __dp4a instructions accumulate 4×4×2=324\times 4\times 2=32 MACs per iteration. Deferred bias correction: result=sw⋅sx⋅(sumi−8⋅sum_x)\text{result}=s_{w}\cdot s_{x}\cdot(\text{sumi}-8\cdot\text{sum\_x}), with sumi=∑jwjuns​xj\text{sumi}=\sum_{j}w_{j}^{\text{uns}}x_{j} (wuns∈[0,15]w^{\text{uns}}\in[0,15]) and sum_x=∑jxj\text{sum\_x}=\sum_{j}x_{j}.

A.3 Flash Decode Attention

The nve_flash_decode_f16 kernel: Block (32,8)=256(32,8)=256 threads, 8 warps per head. Each warp processes a disjoint sequence chunk with online softmax. Replaces: 2 GQA expansion copies + cuBLAS Q​K⊤QK^{\top} + softmax + cuBLAS scores⋅V\text{scores}\cdot V.

Appendix B WikiText-2 Convergence Details

The zero-degradation result reported in Table 9 (Δ=0.00\Delta=0.00 between W4A16 and W4A8 at 50 sequences) raises a natural concern: is this an artifact of insufficient evaluation data, where both strategies happen to agree on a small sample? We address this by examining the running perplexity at every 10-sequence checkpoint.

Table 21 shows the convergence trajectory for Llama-3.2-1B on T4. At 10 sequences, W4A16 and W4A8 differ by just 0.01 PPL (17.70 vs. 17.71). The gap remains ≤0.01\leq 0.01 at every subsequent checkpoint: 20 sequences (Δ=0.01\Delta=0.01), 30 sequences (Δ=0.00\Delta=0.00), 40 sequences (Δ=0.01\Delta=0.01), and 50 sequences (Δ=0.00\Delta=0.00). The non-monotonic PPL trajectory (rising at 20 sequences, then declining) reflects natural variance in WikiText-2 sequence difficulty, some segments contain rare tokens or long-range dependencies that inflate perplexity. Importantly, W4A16 and W4A8 track each other through these fluctuations, confirming that W4A8 does not introduce systematic bias in either direction.

The convergence at Δ=0.00\Delta=0.00 with 50 sequences (12,800 tokens) provides strong evidence that the zero-degradation finding is not a statistical coincidence. If W4A8 introduced even a small systematic bias, it would accumulate across sequences and become visible at this scale. The fact that both strategies converge to exactly 17.51 suggests that the quantization noise from INT8 activations is genuinely below the measurement resolution of WikiText-2 perplexity at this token count.

Appendix C Additional Figures

This appendix collects supplementary visualizations that support the main experimental findings. Each figure provides a different lens on NVE’s behavior across model scales, memory configurations, and evaluation frameworks.

MCAP-driven bit allocation.

Figure 15 shows the per-layer effective bit allocation that results from MCAP’s threshold-based precision assignment. Layers below the τ=0.7\tau=0.7 threshold receive W4A8 dispatch (lower effective bits due to INT8 activation quantization), while outlier layers receive W4A16 (higher effective bits with FP16 activations). The visualization confirms the finding from Table 2: in most architectures, only the final transformer layer exceeds the threshold, producing a nearly uniform W4A8 allocation with a single W4A16 exception. This near-uniformity is why MCAP Mixed achieves nearly identical throughput to uniform W4A8, only one layer out of 16–36 pays the W4A16 cost.

Quality–throughput Pareto analysis.

Figure 16 presents a unified quality vs. throughput view across all model scales using the ABC (Accuracy–Bandwidth–Cost) evaluation framework. Each point represents a (model, quantization strategy) pair, with throughput on the xx-axis and task accuracy on the yy-axis. NVE’s W4A8 configurations consistently occupy the Pareto-optimal frontier: they achieve the highest throughput at each quality level. The figure also shows that the throughput gap between NVE W4A8 and baselines widens at larger model scales, consistent with the bandwidth-bound analysis in Section 4.2. Notably, no baseline configuration reaches the throughput of NVE W4A8 at any quality level for models ≥\geq3B parameters.

Full system comparison.

Figure 17 provides a comprehensive side-by-side comparison of NVE, llama.cpp, and HuggingFace FP16 across saved model-and-budget scenarios, including the larger 8B constrained regimes. Rather than collapsing everything into a single scalar, the figure shows per-scenario task accuracy and marks out-of-memory baselines explicitly. The relevant comparison is scenario-dependent: not only “how accurate is each system” but also “which operating points remain reachable at all.” Viewed this way, NVE’s advantage is not only higher throughput under comfortable budgets but access to tight 3B/8B memory regimes in which baseline systems do not run.

Representative failure examples.

The collapse of aggressive profile-guided quantization is visible directly in the generated text, not only in summary metrics. In the 1B and constrained larger-model failures, the model falls into short repetitive loops or template fragments rather than producing merely lower-quality answers. Table 22 provides representative examples from the raw outputs. The transition is a sharp boundary between degraded but usable and structurally broken operating points.

Failure signature is consistent across configurations.

The three new rows above are from independent BPW-sweep runs at 0.5, 1.0, and 1.5 bits per weight, all with Config C. The failure signature, a short template fragment repeating with minor surface variation, is remarkably stable across bit-widths. This is useful for deployment monitoring: a degenerate repetition-rate detector would catch Config C collapse in a single generation, whereas a perplexity-only metric might miss it (the repeated template is locally high-probability even as the sequence is semantically broken).

Appendix D Proof of the MCAP Recovery Proposition

We restate the proposition for convenience. Let sis_{i} denote the population-level MCAP score for layer i∈{1,…,L}i\in\{1,\ldots,L\} and s^i(N)\hat{s}_{i}^{(N)} its empirical estimate from NN calibration prompts, computed as a sample mean over the NN per-prompt activation statistics. We assume the NN per-prompt statistics behave as iid draws with a sub-Gaussian envelope of parameter σa\sigma_{a}, so that the sample-mean deviation satisfies

Pr[|s^i(N)−si|≥t]≤2exp(−N​t22​σa2).\Pr\!\left[\left|\hat{s}_{i}^{(N)}-s_{i}\right|\geq t\right]\leq 2\exp\!\left(-\frac{Nt^{2}}{2\sigma_{a}^{2}}\right).

This is an idealization: the 12 prompts are curated for topic coverage (Section 3.1), not iid draws, so we treat the bound as a scaling argument rather than an operational guarantee (see “On tightness” below).

Let s(1)≥s(2)≥⋯≥s(L)s_{(1)}\geq s_{(2)}\geq\cdots\geq s_{(L)} be the sorted population scores and Δk:=s(k)−s(k+1)\Delta_{k}:=s_{(k)}-s_{(k+1)} the top-kk gap. Let 𝒯k\mathcal{T}_{k} be the true top-kk set and 𝒯^k(N)\hat{\mathcal{T}}_{k}^{(N)} the empirical one. Then:

Pr[𝒯^k(N)≠𝒯k]≤2k(L−k)⋅exp(−N​Δk28​σa2).\Pr\!\left[\hat{\mathcal{T}}_{k}^{(N)}\neq\mathcal{T}_{k}\right]\leq 2\,k(L-k)\cdot\exp\!\left(-\frac{N\Delta_{k}^{2}}{8\sigma_{a}^{2}}\right).
Proof.

A recovery failure 𝒯^k(N)≠𝒯k\hat{\mathcal{T}}_{k}^{(N)}\neq\mathcal{T}_{k} requires at least one inversion: some pair (i,j)(i,j) with i∈𝒯ki\in\mathcal{T}_{k}, j∉𝒯kj\notin\mathcal{T}_{k}, and s^i(N)<s^j(N)\hat{s}_{i}^{(N)}<\hat{s}_{j}^{(N)}. For this pair, si−sj≥Δks_{i}-s_{j}\geq\Delta_{k} by definition of the top-kk gap, so the inversion requires

(s^i(N)−si)−(s^j(N)−sj)≤−(si−sj)≤−Δk.(\hat{s}_{i}^{(N)}-s_{i})-(\hat{s}_{j}^{(N)}-s_{j})\leq-(s_{i}-s_{j})\leq-\Delta_{k}.

By the triangle inequality, this forces at least one of |s^i(N)−si||\hat{s}_{i}^{(N)}-s_{i}| or |s^j(N)−sj||\hat{s}_{j}^{(N)}-s_{j}| to exceed Δk/2\Delta_{k}/2. The sub-Gaussian tail bounds each such event by 2exp(−NΔk2/8σa2)2\exp(-N\Delta_{k}^{2}/8\sigma_{a}^{2}).

There are at most k⁡(L−k)k(L-k) straddling pairs, and each contributes two deviation events, so a union bound gives

Pr[𝒯^k(N)≠𝒯k]≤2k(L−k)⋅exp(−N​Δk28​σa2).\Pr\!\left[\hat{\mathcal{T}}_{k}^{(N)}\neq\mathcal{T}_{k}\right]\leq 2\,k(L-k)\cdot\exp\!\left(-\frac{N\Delta_{k}^{2}}{8\sigma_{a}^{2}}\right).

The commonly cited specialization to top-1 recovery (k=1k=1) gives prefactor 2​(L−1)2(L-1). ■\blacksquare

Numerical instantiation for Llama-3.1-8B, top-1.

From Table 2, L=32L=32, s(1)=262s_{(1)}=262, s(2)≈146s_{(2)}\approx 14611 1 Second-largest 8B score read from the saved profile JSON; Table 2 reports only the full range (58–262). (second-largest final-block score), giving Δ1≈116\Delta_{1}\approx 116. The empirical per-layer norm standard deviation across the 12 calibration prompts is σa≈64\sigma_{a}\approx 64 (measured directly from the saved profiling run). Then

N​Δ128​σa2=12⋅11628⋅642≈4.9,\frac{N\Delta_{1}^{2}}{8\sigma_{a}^{2}}=\frac{12\cdot 116^{2}}{8\cdot 64^{2}}\approx 4.9,

so the top-1 bound 2​(L−1)​e−4.9≈62⋅0.0074≈0.462(L-1)\,e^{-4.9}\approx 62\cdot 0.0074\approx 0.46 is non-vacuous but loose. For top-kk with larger kk, the k⁡(L−k)k(L-k) prefactor grows and the raw union bound becomes vacuous; tighter constants require assumptions we do not formally verify. The observed split-half top-kk overlap of 1.0 (Table 2) is consistent with a much tighter true concentration; we report it as empirical evidence that the operational behavior is well inside the regime the proposition describes qualitatively.

On tightness.

The proposition gives a qualitatively correct dependency structure (NN scales with σa2/Δk2\sigma_{a}^{2}/\Delta_{k}^{2}) and a conservative constant. The split-half overlap data suggests the true constant is smaller than the union bound predicts, which is expected: Hoeffding-style bounds are famously loose for highly concentrated empirical distributions like the per-layer norm statistics we observe.

Appendix E Reproducibility

Code and data availability.

The full source tree, calibration prompts, captured run logs, and paper source are released under the MIT License at https://github.com/genovationtech/nve. The layout relevant to the claims in this paper is:

  • •

    src/profiler.rs — MCAP profiler (Section 3.1): 12-prompt calibration, per-layer activation variance, importance scoring, 338-byte JSON profile emission.

  • •

    src/importance_cache.rs — architecture-keyed profile cache referenced in Section 3.

  • •

    src/quantize.rs, src/cuda_kernels.rs — W4A8 / W4A16 dispatch and CUDA kernels (Section 3.2).

  • •

    src/decode_graph.rs — CUDA graph-captured decode path (Section 3.2, §CUDA graph capture).

  • •

    src/pager.rs, src/tier.rs, src/paged_model.rs — three-tier (GPU / RAM / SSD) weight pager (Section 3.3).

  • •

    src/arch.rs, src/generic_model.rs — generic transformer front-end covering the eight evaluated architectures (GPT-2 through Qwen2-7.6B).

  • •

    src/cli/ — nve binary entry point (profile / run / bench subcommands).

  • •

    benchmarks/, src/benchmark.rs, src/abc_benchmark.rs — throughput, PPL, HellaSwag, and 8-task harness used for Sections 4.2 and 4.3.

  • •

    evidence/ — dated capture directories (2026-04-12 through 2026-04-18) holding the Modal runner scripts and raw JSON logs for every figure and table, including the cross-silicon profile hash and threshold ablation.

  • •

    tests/, examples/ — integration tests and minimal runnable examples (examples/test_real_model.py, examples/test_tiered_serving.py).

  • •

    docs/ — architecture notes, quantization details, and the streaming profiler design referenced in the main text.

  • •

    paper/mcap.tex — source of this document; the figures/ subtree holds every plot included here.

Hugging Face access tokens in benchmark scripts are read from the HF_TOKEN environment variable; no credentials are committed to the repository.

  • •

    Hardware: GPU experiments on Modal cloud (NVIDIA T4 sm_75 / A10G sm_86). CPU-only experiments on a commodity AMD cloud instance (2 vCPU, 3.8 GB RAM).

  • •

    Software: CUDA 12.1, driver 535.xx, Rust 1.78, Python 3.11. Each saved run records the Modal container image digest.

  • •

    Build: CUDA kernels compiled with nvcc -O3 --use_fast_math -arch=compute_75 into a shared library linked to a release-mode Rust build with CUDA features enabled.

  • •

    Seeds: decode uses greedy (argmax) sampling throughout; no RNG seed is needed for the tok/s, PPL, HellaSwag, or 8-task results. The 12 calibration prompts are a fixed list held constant across runs, not sampled at run time.

  • •

    Determinism: each saved run records the git commit SHA and the Modal image digest; the commit used to generate every figure in the paper is logged. The 338-byte cross-silicon profile referenced in Section 4.6 has SHA-256
    ac4eea60d1675b12bc83e6e7ac2bd6752c3fda90262306a5985fe843ae8fd149.
